Thanks again for the demo last week — Aurum is excited about the latency profile you showed. Before we move to procurement, our legal and infra teams need a few clarifications on the DPA redlines your team provided. High-level asks below:

- Territory carveouts: we need clear language for APAC-only residency for a named tenant and the fallback when APAC capacity is unavailable. Will Redwood commit to onshore-only storage for that tenant (including backups and snapshots)?
- Snapshot TTLs: can Redwood provide a sample TTL matrix showing retention for warm snapshots, cold snapshots, and long-term archives (by region)? We need explicit times for when snapshots are deleted vs when they are archived to long-term storage.
- Proof of deletion: what evidence will you provide if we request confirmation that snapshots and backups were deleted (e.g., wipe logs, job ids, certificate)?

Attached: our standard DPA redlines and a short checklist of required evidentiary artifacts. Can you point us to the clause lines where you propose compromises (or call out which parts are non-negotiable)?

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Jordan is looped earlier for context; looping Marcus (Legal) and Laura (Platform Ops) so we can give you a concrete playbook + draft redlines.

Quick answers up front:
- Onshore residency: we can support APAC-only residency for a named tenant via Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated pool pinned to APAC. That includes snapshots and backups created within the pinned region.
- Fallback behavior: our standard approach is to fail closed (requests blocked) if pinned capacity is unavailable; we can discuss a controlled soft-fallback to a designated region with prior approval and explicit notification.
- Proof of deletion: we provide deletion job IDs, timestamped audit log entries, and a signed deletion certificate for scheduled erasures. We can also provide a monthly deletion manifest for compliance.

Action: Marcus and Laura will propose precise DPA language and a TTL matrix. I attached the latest DPA draft (v3) and a TTL matrix template — please flag any additional columns you need.

I propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the matrix live. Does 10am PT work for you?

Emily — thanks for the note. I reviewed Aurum's redlines and sketched suggested language below (inline summary; redlines to follow in the attached doc):

1) APAC-only residency clause (proposed summary text)
- "Redwood will store and process Customer Data for the Customer's APAC-designated Tenant exclusively within APAC regions designated by the parties, including primary storage, snapshots, and backups, except as permitted under subsection (b)."
- subsection (b): permitted limited cross-border transfers for monitoring/controls when required by law or where Customer provides prior written consent; such transfers will be logged and subject to contractual restrictions.

2) Fallback behavior (preferred approach)
- Default: fail-closed if regional capacity unavailable.
- Optional: a documented soft-fallback with explicit SLA credits if Customer elects (requires configuration during onboarding). We propose a checkbox in the SOW to enable soft-fallback and specify allowed target regions.

3) Snapshot TTL / archival matrix (proposed commitments)
- Warm snapshots: retained 7 days (immediate rollback window), then auto-delete.
- Cold snapshots: retained 30 days; can be archived to long-term (90+ days) upon request and explicit SOW entry.
- Long-term archives: retained per SOW; by default retained 365 days unless otherwise negotiated.

4) Proof of deletion / evidence package
- We will provide deletion job IDs, system audit log entries with immutable timestamps, and an automated deletion manifest (CSV) containing object ids and erasure timestamps. An on-demand certificate (signed) can be produced within 5 business days.

5) Regulatory hold / legal hold carveout
- Redwood will implement holds on a tenant basis; holds will supersede scheduled TTLs until released by Customer or lawful requirement. We ask for a process to notify Redwood of holds in writing and an SLA for acknowledgement.

I've attached a focused redline for the relevant DPA sections and a filled TTL-matrix sample. Two negotiation notes: (1) our default archival behavior is conservative (we don't keep long-term snapshots unless configured), and (2) deletion certificates for short-lived snapshots are standard but for long-term archived media we require an SOW to cover retrieval/wipe costs for air-gapped archival vendors.

Happy to jump on the call. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- For the proof of deletion manifest: can you include object-level checksums and the storage class (warm/cold/archive)? Our auditors want deterministic evidence mapping to backups; if you can include checksums, that closes the loop.

- Archival vendors: can you list the vendors you use for long-term cold storage in APAC and whether those vendors operate under subcontractor NDAs we can review?

If these are acceptable, we can proceed with the redline exchange and aim for procurement to wrap this month. We'll review Marcus's redline PDF tonight and send back a marked copy.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Emily
